text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic receives Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic, stresses need of government reshuffle for success of economic policy.
- Pristina University rector seriously injured in car bomb explosion in Pristina Thursday.

- Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) calls for dialogue between Serbian authorities and the opposition and says mandates in Serbia's local elections should be given to those who won the vote.
- Yugoslav government says activity continues towards normalising Yugoslavia's status in international financial institutions.
- Yugoslav government adopts platform for ex-Yugoslavia succession talks to be held January 22-23 in Brussels. The Yugoslav delegation will be led by Kosta Mihajlovic.

- Yugoslavia's exports in December 1996 stood at $168 million and imports at $396 million. Imports were 53.9 percent higher in 1996 than the previous year and the 1996 trade deficit is $2.2 billion, says statistics office.
- Following meeting Thursday bakers asked government to enable them to purchase flour from commodity reserves at lower prices or they will have to raise bread price.
- Nis city council will be constituted on January 27 at 10 a.m. According to the municipal electoral commission coalition Zajedno has 41 seats, the Socialists 28 and Serbian Radical Party one seat.
- Socialist party of Bosnian Serb republic to organise round table on the issue of the disputed town of Brcko on January 22 in Banja Luka.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Internal political events at end of last year have postponed Yugoslavia's return to international financial organisations, says Vuk Ognjanovic, minister without portfolio.
- All appeals to decision of Belgrade's municipal electoral commission to be sent to first municipal court within 48 hours from reception of decision, says commission chairman Radomir Lazarevic.
NASA BORBA
- European parliament calls on member countries to freeze relations with Yugoslavia until concrete steps are made to implement OSCE recommendations.
- New Democracy party calls for urgent dialogue of parliamentary parties, welcomes recognition of local election ressults in Belgrade, Nis and Lapovo.
- Opposition supporters' protests over election result annulment continue in Belgrade, Nis, Kragujevac and other towns.
- Money supply in Yugoslavia grew by at least 1.2 billion dinars in the last quarter of 1996, 71 percent up on level at end of September, according to federal government sources.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Ethnic Albanian terrorists are becoming increasingly militant in Kosovo, they are now targeting Albanians who have opted to live in Serbia, says commentary.
